sentences.text: 2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor.
Perused the relevant records.

3. The learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that, when the case was posted on 18.9.2024,
the accused was absent and CW1 was present.
CW1 orally made complaint before the learned Magistrate that the accused threatened her through one Payippara Soman.
As per Annexure C Order, bail granted to the accused was cancelled and M.C. was registered to realise the penalty.
Now, the petitioner wants interference in the order.
4. In this matter, offences alleged are under Sections 324 and 498A of the Indian Penal Code and the petitioner herein is none other than the husband of CW1.

Therefore, there shall be a direction to the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Ernakulam, to release the petitioner on bail, by imposing conditions,
on his appearance, within a period of ten days from today.
Meanwhile, execution of the non-bailable warrant issued against the petitioner, stands stayed for a period of ten days.
Proceedings in M.C.No.934/2024 can go on to realise the penalty for forfeiture of bond from the accused and the sureties.
5. The learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the matter would be settled.
Hence, the learned Magistrate can consider settlement by mediation also, if feasible, or to try the case and dispose of the same, as per law.

This Crl.M.C. stands disposed of as above.
Sd/-
